research_updates.title: Current operator factsheet broadens the documented benefit account
research_updates.notes: Meta reports at least $750 million in cumulative data-center investment, at least 275 operational jobs supported and at least $6.4 million in direct funding to Rutherford County-area schools and nonprofits. It also says it pays the full cost of campus energy and town water/wastewater service. These statements remain operator-reported: the profile does not convert them into audited annual spending, direct FTEs, verified rate impacts or metered resource use.

source.title: Meta Forest City Data Center information sheet
source.notes: Undated current operator factsheet reviewed in 2026. It reports more than $750 million of North Carolina data-center investment, more than 275 operational jobs supported and more than $6.4 million of direct funding to Rutherford County-area schools and nonprofits. It also says Meta pays the full cost of campus energy and town water/wastewater service and describes water-efficiency design. These are operator claims, not audited employment, expenditure, rate-impact or metered-resource records.

research_updates.title: State record links a water-line grant to existing and planned jobs
research_updates.notes: The Rural Infrastructure Authority approved a $148,900 grant to the Town of Forest City for an approximately 1,000-foot publicly owned water-line extension serving a new Facebook campus building. The same record reports 100 existing positions and ten planned jobs over two years. The grant, existing-position snapshot and forecast remain separate; approval does not establish final expenditure or realized hiring.

source.title: North Carolina Rural Infrastructure Authority Approves Nearly $3.83 Million in Funding Requests
source.notes: The Rural Infrastructure Authority approval identifies a $148,900 Industrial Development Fund-Utility Account grant to the Town of Forest City for an approximately 1,000-foot publicly owned water-line extension serving a new Facebook campus building. It reports 100 existing positions and a plan for ten additional jobs over two years. The approval does not prove disbursement, final construction cost, realized hiring, worker residence or a complete public-cost account.

research_updates.title: Brownfield reuse adds community context
research_updates.notes: North Carolina DEQ identifies the data center as reuse of a former textile and boat-manufacturing site affected by contamination and vacancy, under a 2012 Brownfields Agreement. The agency's approximately 14% county-revenue statement is not encoded as a quantitative record because the current page gives no measurement date or denominator and the audited annual county series provides the more defensible fiscal evidence.

source.title: North Carolina Brownfields Program success stories - Andale Facebook Data Center
source.publisher: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality
source.notes: The state brownfields profile describes the former Burlington Industries and Tracker Marine site, contamination, vacancy after 2008 and redevelopment under a 2012 Brownfields Agreement. Its statement that Facebook represents approximately 14% of county revenue is retained only as context because the page gives no measurement date or denominator and does not reconcile the claim to the audited county fiscal series.

research_updates.title: Facility-level 2024 electricity, water and Scope 2 rows located
research_updates.notes: Meta's 2025 Environmental Data Index reports Forest City at 535,555 MWh of electricity consumption, 16 megaliters of water withdrawal, zero market-based Scope 2 emissions and 144,104 metric tons CO2e of location-based Scope 2 emissions for 2024. Electricity is normalized in the evidence record. The rounded water and emissions figures remain explicit context because the shared canonical evidence registry has no compatible annual water-withdrawal or facility-emissions metric; they are not treated as audited utility or emissions records.

source.title: Meta 2025 Environmental Data Index
source.notes: Facility tables report Forest City electricity consumption of 535,555 MWh, water withdrawal of 16 megaliters, zero market-based Scope 2 emissions and 144,104 metric tons CO2e of location-based Scope 2 emissions for 2024. Values are rounded to whole displayed units and the methodology permits utility, meter, design-estimate or proxy inputs where applicable. Only electricity is normalized as a canonical source record because the shared evidence metric registry lacks compatible annual water-withdrawal and facility-emissions definitions.

research_updates.title: North Carolina optical-supply agreement is not allocable to Forest City
research_updates.notes: Meta reports a multiyear U.S. agreement with Corning worth up to $6 billion and a manufacturing expansion in Hickory, North Carolina. No public amount is assigned to Forest City, Rutherford County, local vendor payments, or local employment, so the supplier evidence gap remains and no project amount is inferred.

source.title: Investing in American manufacturing to build the infrastructure for AI
source.notes: Meta describes a multiyear agreement with Corning worth up to $6 billion for U.S. data-center optical infrastructure and a Corning expansion in Hickory, North Carolina. The source does not allocate contract value, purchases, employment, or production to the Forest City campus or Rutherford County, so no quantitative project supplier record is created.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Public-source review for the Microsoft facility at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. The exact-site ordinance and permit records are retained separately from later company/county and Greater San Antonio disclosures. Permit value is an administrative construction amount, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and water use is a source projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this building. Actual annual construction spending, worker residence, payroll, vendor payments, operating purchases, recipient-level tax receipts, same-scope public-service cost, electricity use, wastewater, emissions, and annual community transfers remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: DET01-specific direct-evidence follow-up. The operator data sheet supplies current facility-area and rated-power observations at 21005 Lahser Road. The 2014 operator release bounds the initial launch chronology but supplies no quantitative construction, supplier, payroll, community-funding, resource-use or public-cost observation. The values below are source-reported specifications, not audited utilization, expenditure or impact measures. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Public-source follow-up adds one facility-level 2024 electricity observation from Meta's environmental data index. The same source's rounded Forest City water-withdrawal and Scope 2 emissions values remain contextual until compatible canonical metric definitions exist. A North Carolina supplier announcement is retained only as context because its U.S.-wide contract value and Hickory manufacturing expansion cannot be allocated to Forest City or Rutherford County.

modeled_syntheses.label: Modeled annualized capital spending

period.label: From the original campus announcement through the dated 2026 confirmation of the current cumulative investment floor; annualization uses a 10-20 active-year sensitivity

scope.label: Meta Forest City Data Center campus, Rutherford County, NC

interval.interpretation: Low, central and high values are an explicit sensitivity range, not a statistical confidence interval.

parameters.name: reported_cumulative_investment_floor

provenance.detail: Operator-reported cumulative North Carolina data-center investment floor

parameters.transformation: Serves as the broad capital basis before construction-equipment allocation

parameters.name: low_annualization_years

provenance.detail: Long active-construction window used for the low annual flow

parameters.transformation: Divides cumulative capital

parameters.name: central_annualization_years

provenance.detail: Central active-construction window

parameters.transformation: Divides cumulative capital

parameters.name: high_annualization_years

provenance.detail: Short active-construction window used for the high annual flow

parameters.transformation: Divides cumulative capital

modeled_syntheses.confidence_rationale: The calculation is reproducible but relies on transferred public benchmarks or explicit assumptions where direct local observations are unavailable.
modeled_syntheses.decision_relevance: Supplies a comparable annual construction-capital flow without relabeling the cumulative operator total as one-year spending.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Audited annual capital ledger, phase allocations, equipment shares, and replacement-versus-expansion detail

derivation.formula: reported cumulative investment floor ÷ assumed active construction years
assumptions: All transferred coefficients, conversion factors, and allocation shares are exposed as named parameters.

modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Low-confidence completion account for Microsoft San Antonio. Construction scenarios apply explicit 25%-75% construction-eligible shares to the reported greater-than-$840 million real-and-personal-property floor before using the Prince William County benchmark, so IT equipment is not silently treated as building construction. Operating scenarios combine the reported greater-than-75 employee floor with zero, half, or all of the separate 20-job expansion forecast; they are sensitivities, not fulfillment findings. County GDP, employment, and wage gaps are descriptive 2024 benchmark comparisons and are not facility effects. Existing source projections cover fiscal revenue, public support, and facility water demand. No annual net-fiscal estimate is made because verified same-scope recurring receipts and marginal public-service costs are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: DET01 completed contribution account. Source forecasts remain forecasts; modeled construction, supplier, household, resource and comparison values are visibly labeled sensitivity or benchmark scenarios. Personal-property equipment is excluded before construction multipliers. The 2025 tax-account aggregation is paired with an equal same-scope public-cost break-even threshold, not a net-fiscal result. County comparisons are descriptive and noncausal. Direct community funding, measured resource use, realized jobs, supplier payments and actual public costs remain gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Completed contribution-account syntheses for Meta Forest City / Rutherford County. Broad cumulative capital receives an explicit 25-75% construction-eligible allocation before transferred construction benchmarks; operating scenarios translate the 2015 reported-position snapshot with a visible FTE sensitivity; the same-county, same-fiscal-year tax and incentive claims are reconciled before the public-cost break-even threshold; facility water and electricity resource models retain source rounding and scope; supplier and household channels remain separate; and county comparisons are descriptive benchmark gaps rather than causal effects. No net fiscal, audited, or causal result is asserted.
legacy_first_entry_note: Meta establishes operation of the mapped Forest City facility on April 19, 2012. The four source records and three current canonical facilities do not establish a complete county history or conclusively exclude earlier enterprise, government, institutional, or telecom operations.
scope_note: Provisional private-sector research candidate. Owner/operator history, project boundaries and lifecycle require review. Membership does not verify current operation or establish economic impact.
project_description: Meta Forest City is a hyperscale data-center campus in Rutherford County, North Carolina, that opened on April 19, 2012 after redevelopment of a former industrial site. The project account follows the campus from construction and brownfield reuse through operations, later building work, local water infrastructure, community funding, and facility-level resource reporting.
